Hi all —

Thanks, Sara — reviewed Helix’s annotated DPA. High level: we can accept most of the commercial redlines. A few points that need explicit exec-level exception/acknowledgement before we sign:

- Log retention carveout (Section 4.2): Helix requests retention of debug logs for 5 years. Our standard is 1 year — if Helix requires 5 years that’s a policy exception we should document.
- Sub-processor disclosure cadence: Helix asked for quarterly notice; we currently provide 30 days notice and quarterly is acceptable but requires a template addendum.
- HIPAA / BAA: Redwood is willing to sign a separate BAA tied to the DPA scope. We will mark that BAA as limited to the production environment and agreed sub-processors.
- SCCs for EU transfers: we can adopt the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (2024 template) for the limited telemetry subset. I’ve attached our SCCs template.

I’ve uploaded a redlined DPA and a short summary of the exec-level exceptions.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Redlines_v2.pdf; Redwood_SCCs_template_2024.docx; DPA_Exception_Summary.txt

Next steps for internal workflow: Karthik — please confirm the BAA language and any additional security evidence Helix will need (SOC 2 link, CAIQ). Aditya — when Legal and Security sign off, can you approve the non-standard retention exception so we can proceed to signature routing?

Priya Natarajan
Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com
